body:
Fixes #367

**Rebased onto `origin/main` after #370 landed** (`d71ae2e`, part-pin slices, `Fixes #357`); now on `1e535f9`. The old body is superseded — this is the reconciled version.

## What

A part input pin bound more than once on overlapping bits is a compile error. Both sides of a connection state **one rule** through one `claimBits` helper, so the two errors read as the same rule applied twice:

- out (#355, wording unchanged): `Signal "t" bit 0 is driven by more than one part`
- in (#367): `Part "Not16" pin "in" bit 0 is bound by more than one connection`

## What the rebase changed

1. **`claimBits` claims the pin-side slice's bits**, not the whole pin: `conn.internalSlice?.start ?? 0` … `conn.internalSlice?.end ?? inPin.width - 1`. That is the one line the pre-rebase body predicted, and it is the whole of the change.
2. **The whole-vs-sliced overlap is caught.** An unsliced binding claims `[0..width-1]`, so `Not16(in=a, in[0]=b)` — which #370's verifier measured compiling and evaluating **65534 vs 65535** by binding order — now errors at bit 0, in both orderings. This is the same rule `WHOLE_SIGNAL` states on the signal side, spelled out rather than sentinelled: a pin's width is always known from its chip definition, while a signal's may still be waiting to be inferred. One mechanism, not two.
3. **Disjoint bindings still compile and evaluate.** `Or8Way(in[0]=a, in[1]=b)` and the `Not16` halves-swap are #370's tests and are untouched; the new `Not16(in[0..7]=lo, in[8..15]=hi)` test evaluates them (`lo=0x34, hi=0x12` → `~0x1234`).
4. **The `it.todo` is a real test.** It named #357 because `in[0..7]=lo` did not parse; it parses now.
5. **`printHDL`/`externalSlice` rename** absorbed — the #355 branch reads `conn.externalSlice` and its wording and `WHOLE_SIGNAL` handling are byte-identical.

## A partially bound input pin: legal, and the unbound bits read 0

`!boundRanges.has(p.name)` became `coversAnyBit(boundRanges.get(p.name), p.width)` — the same overlap test, run against the pin's own range.

**Decision: partial binding compiles and the unbound bits read 0.** Only a pin that *no* binding lands on is `input pin "x" is not connected`. Evidence, not preference:

- **#370 already established it.** `Or8Way(in[0]=a, in[1]=b)` is green on `main` with bits 2..7 reading 0, asserted in `compileHDL — part-pin slices (#357)`. Erroring on partial coverage would delete that behaviour.
- **The reference simulator is looser still** — `../web-ide/simulator/src/chip/builder.ts` has **no** connectedness pass at all (`checkMultipleAssignments` checks assignment, never coverage). HACER's rule is already stricter; making it stricter again would diverge further, not less.
- **TECS figure A2.2**, reproduced by #370's verifier: `in[0..1]=true, in[3..5]=six, in[7]=true` on an 8-bit pin is `0b10110011` — the book's own example of a partially bound pin whose gaps are 0.

So the check keeps catching the forgotten wire (`And(a=a, out=out)`) and stops objecting to a pin assembled in pieces. One behaviour change falls out and is pinned by a test: a pin whose *only* binding is out of range (`Not16(in[16]=a)`) now reports both `in[16] is out of range` and `input pin "in" is not connected`. Both are true — `in[16]` names no bit of a 16-bit pin — and it only reaches already-invalid HDL.

## Tests — TDD, red first

Red at the rebase base: **7 failed / 32 passed** in `compiler.test.ts` (commit `72bc251`, tests only). The failure output contained the defect itself: `{"out":65534}` vs `{"out":65535}`.

New: whole-pin-vs-sliced overlap (message, part, pin, bit) · its order-independence · overlapping slices naming the first shared bit (`in[0..3]` / `in[2..5]` → bit 2) · disjoint bindings compiling **and evaluating** · a partially bound pin evaluating with 0s in the gap · a pin with nothing bound still rejected · the out-of-range cascade. Kept: all four original #367 tests.

**148 added / 0 removed** in `compiler.test.ts` — no existing assertion removed or loosened. `65 / 13` in `compiler.ts`; the 13 are the inlined driven-range logic that `claimBits` replaced and `connectedInputs`.

## Definition of done — all exit 0

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm run lint` | **0** — typecheck + eslint + layer ratchet: 34 known, **0 new** |
| `pnpm run test:run` | **0** — 137 files, **2181 passed**, 0 todo (`main`: 2170 + 11) |
| `pnpm run build` | **0** — built in 33.66s |
| `pnpm run lint:docs` | **0** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run --project node src/core/hdl` | **0** — 4 files, 146 passed |

**Official Project-1 vectors:** `src/core/testing` + `project1-bottom-up.test.ts` — 6 files, **152 passed**, exit 0. Everything runs in the `node` Vitest project.

## #363 — still easier, and now more so

`claimBits` is the per-bit range algebra #363 needs, shared by both sides and the only place overlap is decided. The rebase made it *more* useful than the pre-rebase version claimed: it now reasons about **pin** bits as well as signal bits, and `overlaps()` is a named primitive both the claim and the coverage check call. #363 wants `reads`/`writes` keyed per bit rather than per signal — it can key `claimBits`-style ranges by signal and reuse `overlaps` verbatim, and `coversAnyBit` is the shape of "is this bit range fully accounted for".

**Out of scope, unchanged:** #371 (external-side bounds checks — `in[16]=a` is still only caught on the internal side), #363, the importer, ADR-0020.
